p2.original: How is the Economy Doing? How Does One Tell?
p2.zh: 经济情况如何? 一个怎么告诉?

p3.original: The 1990s were boom years for the U.S. economy. Beginning in the late 2000s, from 2007 to 2014, economic performance in the U.S. was poor. The economy experienced another period of strong growth between 2014 and 2019, before COVID-19 rocked the world economy in March and April of 2020. What causes the economy to expand or contract? Why do businesses fail when they are making all the right decisions? Why do workers lose their jobs when they are hardworking and productive? Are bad economic times a failure of the market system? Are they a failure of the government? These are all questions of macroeconomics, which we will begin to address in this chapter. We will not be able to answer all of these questions here, but we will start with the basics: How is the economy doing? How can we tell?
p3.zh: 1990年代是美国经济繁荣的年代. 从2000年代后期开始,从2007年到2014年,美国经济表现不佳.2014年至2019年,在COVID-19于2020年3月和4月震撼世界经济之前,经济又经历了另一个强劲增长的时期.是什么导致经济扩张或萎缩? 为什么企业在作出正确决定时会失败? 为什么工人在勤劳和生产时会失去工作?糟糕的经济时代是市场体系的失败吗? 他们是不是政府的一个失败?这些都是宏观经济问题,我们将在本章中开始讨论这些问题。 我们无法在这里回答所有这些问题,但我们首先要谈基本问题:经济如何? 我们怎么知道?

p4.original: The macro economy includes all buying and selling, all production and consumption; everything that goes on in every market in the economy. How can we get a handle on that? The answer begins more than 80 years ago, during the Great Depression. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and his economic advisers knew things were bad—but how could they express and measure just how bad it was? An economist named Simon Kuznets, who later won the Nobel Prize for his work, came up with a way to track what the entire economy is producing. In this chapter, you will learn how the government constructs GDP, how we use it, and why it is so important.
p4.zh: 宏观经济包括所有买卖,所有生产和消费;经济中每个市场的一切继续。 我们怎么才能处理好这件事?答案始于80多年前的大萧条时期.富兰克林·D总统.罗斯福和他的经济顾问们知道事情是糟糕的,但他们怎么能表达和衡量事情有多糟糕呢? 一位名叫西蒙·库兹涅茨的经济学家,他后来因其作品而获得了诺贝尔奖,他想出了一种方法来追踪整个经济正在生产的东西. 在本章中,你会了解政府是如何构建GDP的,我们如何使用GDP,为什么它如此重要.

p11.original: How Well GDP Measures the Well-Being of Society
p11.zh: 国内生产总值如何很好地衡量社会福祉

p12.original: Macroeconomics focuses on the economy as a whole (or on whole economies as they interact). What causes recessions? What makes unemployment stay high when recessions are supposed to be over? Why do some countries grow faster than others? Why do some countries have higher standards of living than others? These are all questions that macroeconomics addresses. Macroeconomics involves adding up the economic activity of all households and all businesses in all markets to obtain the overall demand and supply in the economy. However, when we do that, something curious happens. It is not unusual that what results at the macro level is different from the sum of the microeconomic parts. What seems sensible from a microeconomic point of view can have unexpected or counterproductive results at the macroeconomic level. Imagine that you are sitting at an event with a large audience, like a live concert or a basketball game. A few people decide that they want a better view, and so they stand up. However, when these people stand up, they block the view for other people, and the others need to stand up as well if they wish to see. Eventually, nearly everyone is standing up, and as a result, no one can see much better than before. The rational decision of some individuals at the micro level—to stand up for a better view—ended up as self-defeating at the macro level. This is not macroeconomics, but it is an apt analogy.
p12.zh: 宏观经济学注重整个经济(或相互作用的全经济).是什么原因导致衰退?为何经济衰退应该结束时失业率仍然很高? 为什么有些国家的增长速度比其他国家快? 为什么有些国家的生活水平比其他国家高?这些都是宏观经济所要解决的问题。宏观经济学涉及将所有家庭和所有市场上的所有企业的经济活动相加,以获得经济的总的供求。 然而,当我们这样做时,会发生一些奇怪的事情。宏观一级的结果与微观经济部分的总和不同,这并非不寻常。 从微观经济角度看,似乎明智的做法可能在宏观经济一级产生出乎意料或适得其反的结果。想象一下,你坐在一个有众多观众的活动上,比如现场演唱会或篮球比赛.少数人决定自己想要更好的景色,于是站起来. 然而,当这些人站起来时,他们屏蔽了别人的视野,其他人如果想看到,也需要站立起来.最终,几乎所有人都站起来,因此,没有人能比以前看到更好的东西。 一些个人在微观一级作出理性的决定,以争取更好的观点,在宏观一级被说成是自负。 这不是宏观经济学,而是适当的类比。

p13.original:
Macroeconomics is a rather massive subject. How are we going to tackle it?  illustrates the structure we will use. We will study macroeconomics from three different perspectives:
         What are the macroeconomic goals? (Macroeconomics as a discipline does not have goals, but we do have goals for the macro economy.)
 What are the frameworks economists can use to analyze the macroeconomy?
 Finally, what are the policy tools governments can use to manage the macroeconomy?
p13.zh: 宏观经济学是一个相当广泛的课题。 我们如何解决这个问题? 我们将从三个不同角度研究宏观经济:宏观经济目标是什么?(作为学科的宏观经济没有目标,但我们确实有宏观经济的目标。 ) 框架经济学家可以用什么来分析宏观经济? 最后,政府可以利用哪些政策工具来管理宏观经济?

p14.zh: 宏观经济目标、框架和政策

p16.original:
In thinking about the macroeconomy's overall health, it is useful to consider three primary goals: economic growth, low unemployment, and low inflation.
        Economic growth ultimately determines the prevailing standard of living in a country. Economists measure growth by the percentage change in real (inflation-adjusted) gross domestic product. A growth rate of more than 3% is considered good.
Unemployment, as measured by the unemployment rate, is the percentage of people in the labor force who do not have a job. When people lack jobs, the economy is wasting a precious resource-labor, and the result is lower goods and services produced. Unemployment, however, is more than a statistic—it represents people’s livelihoods. While measured unemployment is unlikely to ever be zero, economists consider a measured unemployment rate of 5% or less low (good).
Inflation is a sustained increase in the overall level of prices, and is measured by the consumer price index. If many people face a situation where the prices that they pay for food, shelter, and healthcare are rising much faster than the wages they receive for their labor, there will be widespread unhappiness as their standard of living declines. For that reason, low inflation—an inflation rate of 1–2%—is a major goal.
p16.zh: 在考虑宏观经济的整体健康状况时,考虑经济增长、低失业率和低通货膨胀这三个主要目标是有益的。经济增长最终决定了一个国家的普遍生活水平。经济学家以实际(经通货膨胀调整的)国内生产总值的百分比变化衡量增长。增长率超过3%被认为是好的。以失业率衡量的失业是劳动力中没有工作的人的百分比。 当人们缺乏工作时,经济正在浪费一个宝贵的资源库,其结果是生产的货物和服务减少。 然而,失业不仅仅是一个统计数字,它代表着人们的生计。 虽然测量失业率不可能永远为零,但经济学家认为测量失业率为5%或更低(良好)。通货膨胀是价格总体水平的持续上升,以消费物价指数衡量。 如果许多人面临食品、住所和保健费用比他们劳动所得工资上涨快得多的局面,那么随着生活水平的下降,就会普遍出现不幸福。 因此,低通货膨胀率——通货膨胀率为1-2——是一个主要目标。

p18.original: As you learn in the micro part of this book, principal tools that economists use are theories and models (see Welcome to Economics! for more on this). In microeconomics, we used the theories of supply and demand. In macroeconomics, we use the theories of aggregate demand (AD) and aggregate supply (AS). This book presents two perspectives on macroeconomics: the Neoclassical perspective and the Keynesian perspective, each of which has its own version of AD and AS. Between the two perspectives, you will obtain a good understanding of what drives the macroeconomy.
p18.zh: 正如你在本书的微观部分所学到的,经济学家使用的主要工具是理论和模型(关于这一点,请参看Welcome to Economics!). 在微观经济学中,我们使用了供求理论. 在宏观经济学中,我们采用总需求(AD)和总供给(AS)的理论. 本书对宏观经济学提出了两个视角:新古典主义视角和凯恩斯主义视角,每个视角都有自己的AD和AS版本. 在这两个角度之间,你会很好地了解什么是宏观经济的驱动力。

p20.original: National governments have two tools for influencing the macroeconomy. The first is monetary policy, which involves managing the money supply and interest rates. The second is fiscal policy, which involves changes in government spending/purchases and taxes.
p20.zh: 国家政府有两种工具来影响宏观经济。首先是货币政策,它涉及管理货币供应和利率。 第二是财政政策,涉及改变政府开支/购买和税收。

p21.zh: 我们将在其他一章或多章中详细解释每个项目。 当你学会这些东西时, 你会发现目标和政策工具几乎每天都在新闻中。

p22.original: Measuring the Size of the Economy: Gross Domestic Product
p22.zh: 衡量经济规模:国内生产总值

p23.original: Macroeconomics is an empirical subject, so the first step toward understanding it is to measure the economy.
p23.zh: 宏观经济学是一个实证问题,所以理解它的第一步是衡量经济。

p24.original: How large is the U.S. economy? Economists typically measure the size of a nation’s overall economy by its gross domestic product (GDP), which is the value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a given year. Measuring GDP involves counting the production of millions of different goods and services—smart phones, cars, music downloads, computers, steel, bananas, college educations, and all other new goods and services that a country produced in the current year—and summing them into a total dollar value. This task is straightforward: take the quantity of everything produced, multiply it by the price at which each product sold, and add up the total. In 2020, the U.S. GDP totaled $20.9 trillion, the largest GDP in the world.
p24.zh: 美国经济有多大?.经济学家通常用国内生产总值(国内总产值)来衡量一国总体经济的规模,而国内生产总值是一国境内在特定年份生产的所有最终货物和服务的价值。衡量GDP需要计算数百万种不同的商品和服务的生产量——智能电话、汽车、音乐下载、计算机、钢铁、香蕉、大学教育以及一个国家本年度生产的所有其他新的商品和服务——并将这些商品和服务合为美元总值。这项任务是直接的:把生产的所有产品的数量,乘以每件产品销售的价格,再加起来。2020年,美国上映.GDP总量为20.9万亿元,是世界上GDP总量最大的国家.

p25.original: Each of the market transactions that enter into GDP must involve both a buyer and a seller. We can measure an economy's GDP either by the total dollar value of what consumers purchase in the economy, or by the total dollar value of what is the country produces. There is even a third way, as we will explain later.
p25.zh: 进入国内总产值的每一项市场交易都必须同时涉及买方和卖方。 我们可以以消费者在经济中购买的美元总值或国家生产的产品的总美元价值来衡量一个经济体的国内生产总值。 还有第三种方法,我们稍后将加以解释。

p26.original: GDP Measured by Components of Demand
p26.zh: 按需求组成部分计量的国内生产总值

p27.original: Who buys all of this production? We can divide this demand into four main parts: consumer spending (consumption), business spending (investment), government spending on goods and services, and spending on net exports. (See the following Clear It Up feature to understand what we mean by investment.)  shows how these four components added up to the GDP in 2020,  (a) shows the levels of consumption, investment, and government purchases over time, expressed as a percentage of GDP, while  (b) shows the levels of exports and imports as a percentage of GDP over time. A few patterns about each of these components are worth noticing.  shows the components of GDP from the demand side.
p27.zh: 谁买的这些作品? 我们可以将这一需求分为四个主要部分:消费支出(消费)、商业支出(投资)、政府在货物和服务方面的支出以及净出口支出。(见以下Clearing It Up的特征来理解投资的含义. ) 说明这四个组成部分如何在2020年与GDP相加,(a) 显示消费水平、投资水平和政府购买水平,以GDP的百分比表示,(b) 显示进出口水平在一段时间内占GDP的百分比。值得注意的是,关于每个组成部分的几个模式都显示了需求方的国内生产总值组成部分。

p28.original: Components of U.S. GDP in 2022: From the Demand Side
p28.zh: 美国的组成部分。2022年的国内生产总值:来自需求方

p30.original: Components of GDP on the Demand Side (in trillions of dollars)
p30.zh: 需求方国内生产总值的组成部分(以万亿美元计)

p50.original: Percentage of Components of U.S. GDP on the Demand Side
p50.zh: 美国各组成部分的百分比。需求方面的国内生产总值

p52.original: What do economists mean by investment, or business spending? In calculating GDP, investment does not refer to purchasing stocks and bonds or trading financial assets. It refers to purchasing new capital goods, that is, new commercial real estate (such as buildings, factories, and stores) and equipment, residential housing construction, and inventories. Inventories that manufacturers produce this year are included in this year’s GDP—even if they are not yet sold. From the accountant’s perspective, it is as if the firm invested in its own inventories. Business investment in 2020 was $3.6 trillion, according to the Bureau of Economic Analysis.
p52.zh: 经济学家是指投资还是商业支出? 在计算GDP时,投资不是指购买股票和债券或交易金融资产. 它是指购买新的资本货物,即新的商业房地产(例如建筑物、工厂和商店)和设备、住宅建筑和库存。制造商今年生产的存货,即使尚未出售,也列入今年的国内生产总值。 从会计师的角度来看,这就像公司投资自己的存货。2020年企业投资3.6万亿元,据经济分析局统计.

p53.original: Components of GDP on the Demand Side
p53.zh: 需求方的国内生产总值组成部分

p54.original: Consumption expenditure by households is the largest component of GDP, accounting for about two-thirds of the GDP in any year. This tells us that consumers’ spending decisions are a major driver of the economy. However, consumer spending is a gentle elephant: when viewed over time, it does not jump around too much, and has increased modestly from about 60% of GDP in the 1960s and 1970s.
p54.zh: 家庭消费支出是国内生产总值的最大部分,占任何一年国内生产总值的三分之二左右。 这告诉我们,消费者的支出决定是经济的主要驱动力。 然而,消费者支出是一头温和的大象:当随着时间的推移而观察时,它不会跳过太多,并且从1960年代和1970年代占GDP的60%左右略有增长.

p55.original: Investment expenditure refers to purchases of physical plant and equipment, primarily by businesses. If Starbucks builds a new store, or Amazon buys robots, they count these expenditures under business investment. Investment demand is far smaller than consumption demand, typically accounting for only about 15–18% of GDP, but it is very important for the economy because this is where jobs are created. However, it fluctuates more noticeably than consumption. Business investment is volatile. New technology or a new product can spur business investment, but then confidence can drop and business investment can pull back sharply.
p55.zh: 投资支出是指主要由企业购买实物厂房和设备. 如果星巴克建了新店,或者亚马逊购买机器人,他们就会把这些支出算在商业投资项下.投资需求远小于消费需求,通常只占国内生产总值的15-18 %,但对于经济非常重要,因为这就是创造就业的地方。 然而,其波动比消费更为明显。商业投资不稳定.新技术或新产品可以刺激企业投资,但随后信心会下降,企业投资会急剧退缩.

p56.original: If you have noticed any of the infrastructure projects (new bridges, highways, airports) launched during the 2009 recession, or if you received a stimulus check during the pandemic-induced recession of 2020–2021, you have seen how important government spending can be for the economy. Government expenditure in the United States is close to 20% of GDP, and includes spending by all three levels of government: federal, state, and local. The only part of government spending counted in demand is government purchases of goods or services produced in the economy. Examples include the government buying a new fighter jet for the Air Force (federal government spending), building a new highway (state government spending), or a new school (local government spending). A significant portion of government budgets consists of transfer payments, like unemployment benefits, veteran’s benefits, and Social Security payments to retirees. The government excludes these payments from GDP because it does not receive a new good or service in return or exchange. Instead they are transfers of income from taxpayers to others. If you are curious about the awesome undertaking of adding up GDP, read the following Clear It Up feature.
p56.zh: 如果你注意到2009年衰退期间启动的基础设施项目(新桥梁、高速公路、机场),或者在2020-2021年大流行引发的衰退期间获得刺激检查,你可以看到政府支出对经济有多重要。 美国的政府支出接近GDP的20%,包括联邦,州,地方三级政府的支出. 政府开支中唯一按需求计算的部分是政府购买经济中生产的商品或服务.例子包括政府为空军购买新的战斗机(联邦政府开支),建造新的高速公路(州政府开支),或新建学校(地方政府开支). 政府预算的很大一部分包括转移支付,如失业福利、退伍军人福利和对退休人员的社会保障支付。 政府将这些付款排除在国内生产总值之外,因为它得不到新的货物或服务作为回报或交换。 相反,它们是纳税人向他人转移收入。 如果你对增加GDP的伟大任务感到好奇,请阅读以下的Clear It Up特征。

p57.zh: 统计人员如何衡量国内总产值?

p58.original: Government economists at the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), within the U.S. Department of Commerce, piece together estimates of GDP from a variety of sources.
p58.zh: 美国经济分析局(BEA)的政府经济学家.商务部,各界对GDP的估计数据进行拼凑.

p59.original: Once every five years, in the second and seventh year of each decade, the Bureau of the Census carries out a detailed census of businesses throughout the United States. In between, the Census Bureau carries out a monthly survey of retail sales. The government adjusts these figures with foreign trade data to account for exports that are produced in the United States and sold abroad and for imports that are produced abroad and sold here. Once every ten years, the Census Bureau conducts a comprehensive survey of housing and residential finance. Together, these sources provide the main basis for figuring out what is produced for consumers.
p59.zh: 人口普查局每五年一次,在每十年的第二年和第七年,对全美的企业进行详细的人口普查.在此期间,人口调查局每月对零售销售情况进行调查。 政府用外贸数据来调整这些数字,以说明在美国生产并在国外销售的出口,以及在国外生产并在这里销售的进口。人口调查局每十年进行一次住房和居民资金综合调查。 这些来源共同为了解为消费者生产的产品提供了主要依据。

p60.original: For investment, the Census Bureau carries out a monthly survey of construction and an annual survey of expenditures on physical capital equipment.
p60.zh: 投资方面,普查局每月对建设情况进行调查,每年对实物资本设备支出情况进行调查.

p61.original: For what the federal government purchases, the statisticians rely on the U.S. Department of the Treasury. An annual Census of Governments gathers information on state and local governments. Because the government spends a considerable amount at all levels hiring people to provide services, it also tracks a large portion of spending through payroll records that state governments and the Social Security Administration collect.
p61.zh: 对于联邦政府购买的东西,统计人员依赖美国.财政部. 政府年度人口普查收集州和地方政府的资料。 由于政府在各级花费了大量资金雇用人员提供服务,因此政府还通过各州政府和社会保障管理局收集的工资记录跟踪很大一部分支出。

p62.original: With regard to foreign trade, the Census Bureau compiles a monthly record of all import and export documents. Additional surveys cover transportation and travel, and make adjustments for financial services that are produced in the United States for foreign customers.
p62.zh: 关于外贸,人口调查局每月汇编所有进出口文件的记录。 其他调查包括运输和旅行,并对美国为外国客户提供的金融服务作出调整。

p63.original: Many other sources contribute to GDP estimates. Information on energy comes from the U.S. Department of Transportation and Department of Energy. The Agency for Health Care Research and Quality collects information on healthcare. Surveys of landlords find out about rental income. The Department of Agriculture collects statistics on farming.
p63.zh: 许多其他来源对国内总产值估计数作出了贡献。能源信息来自美国.交通部与能源部.保健研究和质量局收集保健信息。房东调查会了解租金收入。农业部收集农业统计。

p64.original: All these bits and pieces of information arrive in different forms, at different time intervals. The BEA melds them together to produce GDP estimates on a quarterly basis (every three months). The BEA then "annualizes" these numbers by multiplying by four. As more information comes in, the BEA updates and revises these estimates. BEA releases the GDP “advance” estimate for a certain quarter one month after a quarter. The “preliminary” estimate comes out one month after that. The BEA publishes the “final” estimate one month later, but it is not actually final. In July, the BEA releases roughly updated estimates for the previous calendar year. Then, once every five years, after it has processed all the results of the latest detailed five-year business census, the BEA revises all of the past GDP estimates according to the newest methods and data, going all the way back to 1929.
p64.zh: 所有这些位点和片段的信息以不同的形式,在不同的时间间隔下到达.BEA将它们合并在一起,按季度(每三个月)编制国内总产值估计数。BEA然后通过乘以4来"年度化"这些数字. 随着更多信息的出现,BEA更新并修改了这些估计数.BEA发布四分之一后四分之一的国内生产总值“提前”估计数。“初步”估计数是在一个月之后提出的。BEA在一个月后公布“最后”估计数,但实际上不是最后估计数。7月,BEA公布了上一个日历年的大致最新估计数。 然后,在经过对最新详细五年商业普查结果的处理后,每五年一次,BEA根据最新的方法和数据修订过去所有GDP估计,一直追溯到1929年.

p66.original: When thinking about the demand for domestically produced goods in a global economy, it is important to count spending on exports—domestically produced goods that a country sells abroad. Similarly, we must also subtract spending on imports—goods that a country produces in other countries that residents of this country purchase. The GDP net export component is equal to the dollar value of exports (X) minus the dollar value of imports (M), (X – M). We call the gap between exports and imports the trade balance. If a country’s exports are larger than its imports, then a country has a trade surplus. In the United States, exports typically exceeded imports in the 1960s and 1970s, as (b) shows.
p66.zh: 在考虑全球经济对国内生产商品的需求时,必须把出口开支计算在内,即一国在国外销售的国内生产商品。 同样,我们还必须减少进口开支——一国在其他国家生产的货物,供该国居民购买。国内总产值净出口部分等于出口的美元价值(X)减去进口的美元价值(M),(X-M)。 我们把进出口之间的差距称为贸易平衡。 如果一个国家的出口大于其进口,那么一个国家就有贸易顺差. 如(b)所示,美国1960年代和1970年代的出口通常超过进口。

p67.original: Since the early 1980s, imports have typically exceeded exports, and so the United States has experienced a trade deficit in most years. The trade deficit grew quite large in the late 1990s and in the mid-2000s.  (b) also shows that imports and exports have both risen substantially in recent decades, even after the declines during the Great Recession between 2008 and 2009. As we noted before, if exports and imports are equal, foreign trade has no effect on total GDP. However, even if exports and imports are balanced overall, foreign trade might still have powerful effects on particular industries and workers by causing nations to shift workers and physical capital investment toward one industry rather than another.
p67.zh: 自1980年代初以来,进口通常超过出口,因此美国在大多数年份都经历了贸易逆差.贸易赤字在1990年代末和2000年代中期增长相当大。(b) 也表明,近几十年来,即使在2008年至2009年大衰退期间的下降之后,进口和出口都大幅上升。 正如我们以前指出的,如果进出口相等,外贸对国内生产总值总额没有影响。 然而,即使进出口总体上是平衡的,对外贸易仍可能对特定行业和工人产生强有力的影响,使各国将工人和实物资本投资转向一个行业而不是另一个行业。

p100.original: In thinking about what is produced in the economy, many non-economists immediately focus on solid, long-lasting goods, like cars and computers. By far the largest part of GDP, however, is services. Moreover, services have been a growing share of GDP over time. A detailed breakdown of the leading service industries would include healthcare, education, and legal and financial services. It has been decades since most of the U.S. economy involved making solid objects. Instead, the most common jobs in a modern economy involve a worker looking at pieces of paper or a computer screen; meeting with co-workers, customers, or suppliers; or making phone calls.
p100.zh: 在思考经济中生产的东西时,许多非经济主义者立即关注固态,耐久的商品,如汽车和计算机. 然而,迄今为止,服务业是国内生产总值的最大部分。 此外,随着时间的推移,服务业在国内生产总值中所占的份额越来越大。 主要服务业的详细分类将包括保健、教育以及法律和金融服务。 美国大部分经济都涉及制造坚固的物品,至今已有几十年. 相反,现代经济中最常见的工作涉及工人看纸片或电脑屏幕;与同事、顾客或供应商会面;或打电话。

p101.original: Even within the overall category of goods, long-lasting durable goods like cars and refrigerators are about the same share of the economy as short-lived nondurable goods like food and clothing. The category of structures includes everything from homes, to office buildings, shopping malls, and factories. Inventories is a small category that refers to the goods that one business has produced but has not yet sold to consumers, and are still sitting in warehouses and on shelves. The amount of inventories sitting on shelves tends to decline if business is better than expected, or to rise if business is worse than expected.
p101.zh: 即使在商品的总类别中,汽车和冰箱等耐久商品在经济中的份额与衣食等短寿命不可持久商品大致相同.建筑的类别包括从住宅,到办公楼,购物中心,以及工厂的一切.库存是一个小类,是指一家企业已经生产但尚未出售给消费者的商品,目前仍存放在仓库和货架上。 如果业务情况好于预期,则库存量往往会减少,如果业务情况差于预期,则库存量则会增加。

p102.original: Another Way to Measure GDP: The National Income Approach
p102.zh: 衡量国内生产总值的另一种方法:国民收入办法

p103.original: GDP is a measure of what is produced in a nation. The primary way GDP is estimated is with the Expenditure Approach we discussed above, but there is another way.  Everything a firm produces, when sold, becomes revenues to the firm. Businesses use revenues to pay their bills: Wages and salaries for labor, interest and dividends for capital, rent for land, profit to the entrepreneur, etc. So adding up all the income produced in a year provides a second way of measuring GDP. This is why the terms GDP and national income are sometimes used interchangeably. The total value of a nation’s output is equal to the total value of a nation’s income.
p103.zh: 国内生产总值是衡量一个国家生产的产品。估计国内生产总值的主要方式是上文讨论的支出方法,但还有另一种方式。 一个公司生产的一切,一旦出售,就成为公司的收入.企业利用收入支付账单:劳动工资和工资,资本利息和股息,土地租金,企业主利润等. 因此,将一年中产生的所有收入加起来,提供了衡量GDP的第二种方法. 这就是为什么有时可以互换使用国内生产总值和国民收入这两个术语。一国产出的总价值等于一国收入的总价值。

p105.original: We define GDP as the current value of all final goods and services produced in a nation in a year. What are final goods? They are goods at the furthest stage of production at the end of a year. Statisticians who calculate GDP must avoid the mistake of double counting, in which they count output more than once as it travels through the production stages. For example, imagine what would happen if government statisticians first counted the value of tires that a tire manufacturer produces, and then counted the value of a new truck that an automaker sold that contains those tires. In this example, the statisticians would have counted the value of the tires twice-because the truck's price includes the value of the tires.
p105.zh: 我们把国内生产总值定义为一国一年内生产的所有最终商品和服务的现值。最终的货是什么?它们是一年末处于生产最远阶段的货物。计算GDP的统计员必须避免双重计算的错误,在重复计算中,他们在经过生产阶段时不止一次地计算产出. 例如,想象一下,如果政府统计人员首先计算轮胎制造商生产的轮胎的价值,然后计算汽车制造商出售的装有轮胎的新卡车的价值,那么会发生什么。 在这个例子中,统计人员本来会计算轮胎的价值两次——因为卡车的价格包括轮胎的价值.

p106.original: To avoid this problem, which would overstate the size of the economy considerably, government statisticians count just the value of final goods and services in the chain of production that are sold for consumption, investment, government, and trade purposes. Statisticians exclude intermediate  goods, which are goods that go into producing other goods, from GDP calculations. From the example above, they will only count the Ford truck's value. The value of what businesses provide to other businesses is captured in the final products at the end of the production chain.
p106.zh: 为避免这一问题,政府统计人员只计算为消费、投资、政府和贸易目的销售的生产链中最终商品和服务的价值,因为这一问题将大大夸大经济规模。统计人员将中间货物,即生产其他货物的货物,排除在国内生产总值的计算之外。 从上面的例子来看,他们只会计算福特卡车的价值.企业向其他企业提供的价值在生产链末端的最终产品中得到体现。

p107.original: The concept of GDP is fairly straightforward: it is just the dollar value of all final goods and services produced in the economy in a year. In our decentralized, market-oriented economy, actually calculating the more than $21 trillion-dollar U.S. GDP—along with how it is changing every few months—is a full-time job for a brigade of government statisticians.
p107.zh: 国内生产总值的概念相当直截了当:它只是一年中经济中所有最终商品和服务的美元价值。 在我们分散的,面向市场的经济中, 实际计算出21万亿美元以上的美国。 除了每几个月一次的GDP变化之外,一个政府统计人员大队的全职工作。

p121.original: Other Ways to Measure the Economy

p122.original: Besides GDP, there are several different but closely related ways of measuring the size of the economy. We mentioned above that we can think of GDP as total production and as total purchases. We can also think of it as total income since anything one produces and sells yields income.
p122.zh: 除了国内生产总值之外,衡量经济规模还有几种不同但密切相关的方法。 我们在上面提到,我们可以把国内生产总值看作是总产量和总购买量。 我们还可以把它看作是总收入,因为任何人生产和销售都会产生收入。

p123.original: One of the closest cousins of GDP is the gross national product (GNP). GDP includes only what a country produces within its borders. GNP adds what domestic businesses and labor abroad produces, and subtracts any payments that foreign labor and businesses located in the United States send home to other countries. In other words, GNP is based more on what a country's citizens and firms produce, wherever they are located, and GDP is based on what happens within a certain country's geographic boundaries. For the United States, the gap between GDP and GNP is relatively small; in recent years, only about 0.2%. For small nations, which may have a substantial share of their population working abroad and sending money back home, the difference can be substantial.
p123.zh: 国内生产总值中最接近的表兄弟之一是国民生产总值。国内生产总值仅包括一国境内生产的产品。国产总值增加了国内企业和国外劳工生产的产品,并减去外国劳工和设在美国的企业向其他国家支付的任何款项。换句话说,国产总值更多地以一国公民和公司在任何地方生产的东西为基础,而国内生产总值则以某一国家地理边界内发生的事情为基础。 就美国而言,国内生产总值与国民生产总值之间的差距相对较小;近年来,只有0.2%左右。 对小国来说,这种差别可能很大,因为这些国家可能有相当一部分人口在国外工作,并且将钱汇回本国。

p124.original: We calculate net national product (NNP) by taking GNP and then subtracting the value of how much physical capital is worn out, or reduced in value because of aging, over the course of a year. The process by which capital ages and loses value is called depreciation. We can further subdivide NNP into national income, which includes all income to businesses and individuals, and personal income, which includes only income to people.
p124.zh: 我们计算净国民产值时,采用国产总值,然后减去一年中有多少实物资本耗竭或因老化而减少的价值。资本老化和价值损失的过程称为折旧. 我们可以进一步将NNP细分为国民收入,包括企业和个人的所有收入,以及个人收入,仅包括人民的收入。

p125.original: The gross national income (GNI) includes the value of all goods and services produced by people from a country—whether in the country or not. Unlike the other methods, GNI essentially measures the wealth of a nation because it focuses on income, not output. As you will see in the discussion regarding global economic diversity, the World Bank now uses GNI to classify nations according to economic status.
p125.zh: 国民总收入包括一国人民生产的所有货物和服务的价值,不论是否在该国。与其他方法不同,国民总收入主要衡量一个国家的财富,因为它注重收入,而不是产出。 正如大家在讨论全球经济多样性时所看到的那样,世界银行现在利用国民总收入按经济状况对国家进行分类。

p126.original: For practical purposes, it is not vital to memorize these definitions. However, it is important to be aware that these differences exist and to know what statistic you are examining, so that you do not accidentally compare, say, GDP in one year or for one country with GNP or NNP in another year or another country. To get an idea of how these calculations work, follow the steps in the following Work It Out feature.
p126.zh: 为了实际目的,不一定要记住这些定义。 然而,必须意识到这些差异的存在,并知道你们正在审查哪些统计数据,以便你们不会意外地比较,比如说,一年中的国内生产总值,或者一个国家有国产总值,或者另一个年份或另一个国家有NNP。 为了了解这些计算是如何工作的, 遵循下面的“工作它”功能中的步骤。

p149.original: Economists generally express the size of a nation’s economy as its gross domestic product (GDP), which measures the value of the output of all final goods and services produced within the country in a year. Economists measure GDP by taking the quantities of all goods and services produced, multiplying them by their prices, and summing the total. Since GDP measures what is bought and sold in the economy, we can measure it either by the sum of what is purchased in the economy or what is produced.
p149.zh: 经济学家一般将一个国家的经济规模作为国内生产总值(国内总产值)来表示,它衡量该国一年内生产的所有最终货物和服务的产出价值。经济学家用生产的所有货物和服务的数量来衡量国内总产值,用其价格乘以其价格,然后汇总总和。 由于国内总产值衡量的是经济中买卖的什么,我们可以以经济中购买的东西的总和或生产的东西来衡量。

p150.original: We can divide demand into consumption, investment, government, exports, and imports. We can divide what is produced in the economy into durable goods, nondurable goods, services, structures, and inventories. To avoid double counting, GDP counts only final output of goods and services, not the production of intermediate goods or the value of labor in the chain of production.
p150.zh: 我们可以把需求分为消费、投资、政府、出口和进口。 我们可以把经济生产的产品分为耐用商品、非耐用商品、服务、结构和库存。为了避免双重计算,GDP只计算商品和服务的最终产出,而不是中间产品的生产或生产链中的劳动力价值。

p174.original: Adjusting Nominal Values to Real Values

p175.original: When examining economic statistics, there is a crucial distinction worth emphasizing. The distinction is between nominal and real measurements, which refer to whether or not inflation has distorted a given statistic. Looking at economic statistics without considering inflation is like looking through a pair of binoculars and trying to guess how close something is: unless you know how strong the lenses are, you cannot guess the distance very accurately. Similarly, if you do not know the inflation rate, it is difficult to figure out if a rise in GDP is due mainly to a rise in the overall level of prices or to a rise in quantities of goods produced. The nominal value of any economic statistic means that we measure the statistic in terms of actual prices that exist at the time. The real value refers to the same statistic after it has been adjusted for inflation. Generally, it is the real value that is more important.
p175.zh: 在审查经济统计时,有一个关键的区别值得强调。区别在于名义计量和真实计量,后者指通货膨胀是否扭曲了某一统计。 在不考虑通货膨胀的情况下观察经济统计, 就像是透过双望远镜来观察, 并试图猜测事物有多近:除非你知道透镜有多强, 否则你无法非常准确地猜测距离。 同样,如果你不知道通货膨胀率,那么很难确定国内生产总值的上升是主要由于总的物价水平的上升,还是由于生产的货物数量的上升。任何经济统计的面值意味着,我们以当时存在的实际价格来衡量统计。实际值是指通货膨胀调整后得出的相同统计数据。一般来说,更重要的是真正的价值。

p222.original: If an unwary analyst compared nominal GDP in 1960 to nominal GDP in 2010, it might appear that national output had risen by a factor of more than 38 over this time (that is, GDP of $20.9 trillion in 2020 divided by GDP of $543 billion in 1960 = 38). This conclusion would be highly misleading. Recall that we define nominal GDP as the quantity of every final good or service produced multiplied by the price at which it was sold, summed up for all goods and services. In order to see how much production has actually increased, we need to extract the effects of higher prices on nominal GDP. We can easily accomplish this using the GDP deflator.

p374.original: The most significant human problem associated with recessions (and their larger, uglier cousins, depressions) is that a slowdown in production means that firms need to lay off or fire some of their workers. p375.original: lists the pattern of recessions and expansions in the U.S. economy since 1900. We call the highest point of the economy, before the recession begins, the peak. Conversely, the lowest point of a recession, before a recovery begins, is the trough. Thus, a recession lasts from peak to trough, and an economic upswing runs from trough to peak. We call the economy's movement from peak to trough and trough to peak the business cycle. It is intriguing to notice that the three longest trough-to-peak expansions of the twentieth century have happened since 1960. The most recent recession was caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. It started in February 2020 and ended formally in May 2020. This was the most severe recession since the 1930s Great Depression, but also the shortest. The previous recession, called the Great Recession, was also very severe and lasted about 18 months. The expansion starting in June 2009, the trough from the Great Recession, was the longest on record—ending 128 months with the pandemic-induced recession.

p496.zh: 国家间国内总产值比较

p497.original: It is common to use GDP as a measure of economic welfare or standard of living in a nation. When comparing the GDP of different nations for this purpose, two issues immediately arise. First, we measure a country's GDP in its own currency: the United States uses the U.S. dollar; Canada, the Canadian dollar; most countries of Western Europe, the euro; Japan, the yen; Mexico, the peso; and so on. Thus, comparing GDP between two countries requires converting to a common currency. A second issue is that countries have very different numbers of people. For instance, the United States has a much larger economy than Mexico or Canada, but it also has almost three times as many people as Mexico and nine times as many people as Canada. Thus, if we are trying to compare standards of living across countries, we need to divide GDP by population.
p497.zh: 将国内生产总值作为衡量一个国家的经济福利或生活水平的尺度是常见的。 在为此目的比较不同国家的国内生产总值时,立即出现了两个问题。 首先,我们用本国货币衡量一个国家的GDP:美国使用美元;加拿大,加拿大美元;西欧大多数国家,欧元;日本,日元;墨西哥,比索等等. 因此,比较两国的国内生产总值需要转换为共同货币。 第二个问题是,各国的人数大不相同。 例如,美国的经济比墨西哥或加拿大大得多,但是它的人口几乎是墨西哥的三倍,是加拿大的九倍。 因此,如果我们试图比较各国之间的生活水平,我们需要按人口划分国内生产总值。

p499.original: To compare the GDP of countries with different currencies, it is necessary to convert to a “common denominator” using an exchange rate, which is the value of one currency in terms of another currency. We express exchange rates either as the units of country A’s currency that need to be traded for a single unit of country B’s currency (for example, Japanese yen per British pound), or as the inverse (for example, British pounds per Japanese yen). We can use two types of exchange rates for this purpose, market exchange rates and purchasing power parity (PPP) equivalent exchange rates. Market exchange rates vary on a day-to-day basis depending on supply and demand in foreign exchange markets. PPP-equivalent exchange rates provide a longer run measure of the exchange rate. For this reason, economists typically use PPP-equivalent exchange rates for GDP cross country comparisons. We will discuss exchange rates in more detail in Exchange Rates and International Capital Flows. The following Work It Out feature explains how to convert GDP to a common currency.
p499.zh: 为了比较各国不同货币的国内生产总值,有必要采用汇率,即一种货币对另一种货币的价值,转换成“共同分母”。 我们表示的汇率要么是A国货币单位,需要用B国货币单单位(例如,日元/英磅)进行交易,要么是反向(例如,英磅/日元). 为此,我们可以采用两种汇率,即市场汇率和购买力平价等价汇率。市场汇率因外汇市场的供求情况而异。购买力平价等值的汇率是长期汇率的衡量尺度。 因此,经济学家通常使用购买力平价等值的汇率进行国与国之间的GDP比较。 我们将更详细地讨论汇率和国际资本流动。 以下的Work It Out功能解释了如何将GDP转换为共同货币.

One caveat: For reasons we will discuss shortly, GDP per capita can give us only a rough idea of the differences in living standards across countries.

p621.original: The world’s high-income nations—including the United States, Canada, the Western European countries, and Japan—typically have GDP per capita in the range of $20,000 to $50,000. Middle-income countries, which include much of Latin America, Eastern Europe, and some countries in East Asia, have GDP per capita in the range of $6,000 to $12,000. The world's low-income countries, many of them located in Africa and Asia, often have GDP per capita of less than $2,000 per year.
p621.zh: 世界上的高收入国家——包括美国、加拿大、西欧国家和日本——的人均国内生产总值通常在20,000至50,000美元之间。中等收入国家,包括拉丁美洲、东欧和东亚一些国家,人均国内生产总值在6 000至12 000美元之间。世界上的低收入国家,其中许多位于非洲和亚洲,每年的人均国内总产值往往不到2 000美元。

p623.original: Since we measure GDP in a country’s currency, in order to compare different countries’ GDPs, we need to convert them to a common currency. One way to do that is with the exchange rate, which is the price of one country’s currency in terms of another. Once we express GDPs in a common currency, we can compare each country’s GDP per capita by dividing GDP by population. Countries with large populations often have large GDPs, but GDP alone can be a misleading indicator of a nation's wealth. A better measure is GDP per capita.
p623.zh: 既然我们用一个国家的货币衡量GDP,为了比较不同国家的GDP,我们需要把它们转换成共同的货币.这样做的方法之一是汇率,汇率是一国货币对另一国货币的价格。 一旦我们以共同货币表示GDP,我们就可以通过将GDP除以人口来比较每个国家的人均GDP.人口众多的国家往往拥有大量的国内生产总值,但仅靠国内生产总值就可以误导一个国家的财富。衡量人均国内生产总值的更好方法。

p625.original: Is it possible for GDP to rise while at the same time per capita GDP is falling? Is it possible for GDP to fall while per capita GDP is rising?
p625.zh: 在人均国内生产总值下降的同时,能否提高国内生产总值? 在人均国内生产总值上升的同时,国内生产总值是否可能下降?

p626.original: Yes. The answer to both questions depends on whether GDP is growing faster or slower than population. If population grows faster than GDP, GDP increases, while GDP per capita decreases. If GDP falls, but population falls faster, then GDP decreases, while GDP per capita increases.
p626.zh: 对 这两个问题的答案取决于国内生产总值的增长是否快于人口。 如果人口增长快于GDP,GDP就会增加,而人均GDP则会下降. 如果国内总产值下降,但人口下降更快,则国内总产值下降,而人均国内总产值则增加。

That is, 1,107,689 million francs / 284.681 francs per dollar / 4.862 million people = $800.28 GDP per capita.
p628.zh: 从中非共和国以法郎计算的国内生产总值开始。 除以汇率换算成美元,然后按人口除以获得人均数字。即11.76.89亿法郎/每美元284.681法郎/4.862亿人口=人均国内生产总值800.28美元。

p630.original: What are the two main difficulties that arise in comparing different countries's GDP?
p630.zh: 在比较不同国家的国内生产总值时出现的两个主要困难是什么?

p632.original: Cross country comparisons of GDP per capita typically use purchasing power parity equivalent exchange rates, which are a measure of the long run equilibrium value of an exchange rate. In fact, we used PPP equivalent exchange rates in this module. Why could using market exchange rates, which sometimes change dramatically in a short period of time, be misleading?
p632.zh: 人均国内总产值的跨国比较通常采用购买力平价等值汇率,这是衡量汇率长期平衡值的一个尺度。 事实上,我们在这个模块中使用了购买力平价等值的汇率。 为什么使用市场汇率,有时在短时间内发生剧烈变化,是误导呢?

p633.original: Why might per capita GDP be only an imperfect measure of a country’s standard of living?
p633.zh: 为什么人均国内生产总值只是衡量一个国家生活水平的不完善尺度?

p635.original: Ethiopia has a GDP of $8 billion (measured in U.S. dollars) and a population of 55 million. Costa Rica has a GDP of $9 billion (measured in U.S. dollars) and a population of 4 million. Calculate the per capita GDP for each country and identify which one is higher.
p635.zh: 埃塞俄比亚GDP为80亿美元(以美元计算),人口为5500万. 哥斯达黎加的国内生产总值为90亿美元(以美元衡量),人口为400万。计算每个国家的人均GDP,并找出哪个更高.

p636.original: In 1980, Denmark had a GDP of $70 billion (measured in U.S. dollars) and a population of 5.1 million. In 2000, Denmark had a GDP of $160 billion (measured in U.S. dollars) and a population of 5.3 million. By what percentage did Denmark’s GDP per capita rise between 1980 and 2000?
p636.zh: 1980年,丹麦GDP为700亿美元(以美元衡量),人口为510万.2000年,丹麦GDP为1,600亿美元(以美元衡量),人口为530万. 在1980年至2000年期间,丹麦的人均国内生产总值上升了多少百分比?

p637.original: The Czech Republic has a GDP of 1,800 billion koruny. The exchange rate is 25 koruny/U.S. dollar. The Czech population is 20 million. What is the GDP per capita of the Czech Republic expressed in U.S. dollars?
p637.zh: 捷克共和国的国内生产总值为18亿克朗。汇率为25克朗/美元。捷克人口为2000万. 捷克共和国的人均国内生产总值以美元表示是什么?

p638.original: How Well GDP Measures the Well-Being of Society
p638.zh: 国内生产总值如何很好地衡量社会福祉

p639.original: The level of GDP per capita clearly captures some of what we mean by the phrase “standard of living.” Most of the migration in the world, for example, involves people who are moving from countries with relatively low GDP per capita to countries with relatively high GDP per capita.
p639.zh: 人均GDP水平清楚地反映了“生活水平”这一短语中的一些含义。 例如,世界上大多数移民都从人均GDP相对较低的国家迁移到人均GDP相对较高的国家。

p640.original: “Standard of living” is a broader term than GDP. While GDP focuses on production that is bought and sold in markets, standard of living includes all elements that affect people’s well-being, whether they are bought and sold in the market or not. To illuminate the difference between GDP and standard of living, it is useful to spell out some things that GDP does not cover that are clearly relevant to standard of living.
p640.zh: “生活标准”一词比国内生产总值要宽泛。国内生产总值侧重于市场买卖的生产,而生活水平则包括影响人民福祉的所有要素,无论是否在市场买卖。 为了阐明国内生产总值与生活水平之间的差异,有必要阐明国内生产总值没有涵盖的与生活水平明显相关的一些事情。

p641.original: Limitations of GDP as a Measure of the Standard of Living
p641.zh: 作为生活水平衡量尺度的国内生产总值的局限性

p642.original: GDP measures economic activity, not all activity. As a result, economists like Kate Raworth see it as a somewhat outdated and limited indication of well-being and prosperity. While GDP measures output of work done at home, as well as spending on travel, it doesn't capture unpaid work or leisure time. So, two countries may have equal GDP, but one nation's workers may have an average workday of eight hours, while the other has an average workday of twelve hours. In that case, is their equal GDP truly measuring the prosperity of those nations? The GDP per capita of the U.S. economy is larger than the GDP per capita of Germany, as  showed, but does that prove that the standard of living in the United States is higher? Not necessarily, since it is also true that the average U.S. worker works several hundred hours more per year more than the average German worker. Calculating GDP does not account for the German worker’s extra vacation weeks.
p642.zh: GDP衡量的是经济活动,而不是所有的活动。 因此,凯特·拉沃思等经济学家认为这在某种程度上是过时的,有限的福利和繁荣的表示. 虽然GDP衡量的是在家完成的工作的产出,以及旅行开支,但是它并没有抓住无报酬的工作或闲暇时间. 因此,两个国家的国内生产总值可能相等,但一个国家的工人平均工作日可能为8小时,而另一个国家的平均工作日为12小时。 在这种情况下,它们的平等国内总产值是否真正衡量了这些国家的繁荣? 美国经济的人均GDP大于德国的人均GDP,如上所示,但这是否证明美国的生活水平更高?不一定,因为美国工人的年平均工作时间也比德国工人的年平均多几百小时。计算GDP并不包括德国工人的额外休假周。

p643.original: While GDP includes what a country spends on environmental protection, healthcare, and education, it does not include actual levels of environmental cleanliness, health, and learning. GDP includes the cost of buying pollution-control equipment, but it does not address whether the air and water are actually cleaner or dirtier. GDP includes spending on medical care, but does not address whether life expectancy or infant mortality have risen or fallen. Similarly, it counts spending on education, but does not address directly how much of the population can read, write, or do basic mathematics.
p643.zh: 虽然国内生产总值包括一个国家在环境保护、保健和教育方面的开支,但它不包括环境清洁、健康和学习的实际水平。国内生产总值包括购买污染控制设备的费用,但并未涉及空气和水实际上是否更清洁或更脏的问题。国内生产总值包括医疗开支,但没有解决预期寿命或婴儿死亡率是否上升或下降的问题。 同样,它把教育开支计算在内,但没有直接解决人口中有多少人能够读、写或做基本数学的问题。

p644.original: GDP includes production that is exchanged in the market, but it does not cover production that is not exchanged in the market. For example, hiring someone to mow your lawn or clean your house is part of GDP, but doing these tasks yourself is not part of GDP. One remarkable change in the U.S. economy in recent decades is the growth in women’s participation in  the labor force.  As of 1970, only about 42% of women participated in the paid labor force. By the second decade of the 2000s, nearly 60% of women participated in the paid labor force according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. As women are now in the labor force, many of the services they used to produce in the non-market economy like food preparation and child care have shifted to some extent into the market economy, which makes the GDP appear larger even if people actually are not consuming more services. However, as Raworth points out and was explored in the chapter on the labor market, even women who are fully employed expend significant effort (generally more than men) in raising children and maintaining a home. Raworth advocates that economic measures include monetized and un-monetized goods and services, so that the status and contributors to each economy are more accurate.
p644.zh: GDP包括市场中交换的生产,但不包括市场中不交换的生产. 例如,雇人修剪草坪或清理房屋是GDP的一部分,但自己完成这些任务不是GDP的一部分. 最近几十年美国经济的一个显著变化是女性加入劳动力队伍的增长。 截至1970年,只有大约42%的妇女参加了有薪劳动力队伍。 根据劳工统计局的数据,到2000年代第二个十年,近60%的妇女参加了有薪劳动力。 由于妇女现在已进入劳动力队伍,她们在非市场经济中生产的许多服务,例如食品准备和儿童保育,在某种程度上已转移到市场经济,这使得即使人们实际上没有消费更多的服务,国内生产总值也显得更大。 然而,正如Raworth指出并在关于劳动力市场的一章中探讨的那样,即使是被充分雇用的妇女也在抚养子女和维持家庭方面付出了很大努力(一般比男子多)。 拉沃斯主张经济措施包括货币化和无货币化的商品和服务,这样每个经济体的地位和贡献都更加准确.

p645.original: GDP has nothing to say about the level of inequality in society. GDP per capita is only an average. When GDP per capita rises by 5%, it could mean that GDP for everyone in the society has risen by 5%, or that GDP of some groups has risen by more while that of others has risen by less—or even declined. GDP also has nothing in particular to say about the amount of variety available. If a family buys 100 loaves of bread in a year, GDP does not care whether they are all white bread, or whether the family can choose from wheat, rye, pumpernickel, and many others—it just looks at the total amount the family spends on bread.
p645.zh: 国内生产总值对社会的不平等程度没有任何可说的。人均GDP仅为平均水平. 当人均国内生产总值上升5%时,就可能意味着社会中每个人的国内生产总值都上升了5%,或者某些群体的国内生产总值上升了更多,而另一些群体的国内生产总值则上升了更少,甚至有所下降。国内生产总值对于现有品种的数量也没有任何特别的可言。 如果一个家庭一年内购买了100块面包,GDP就不在乎它们是否都是白面包,或者家庭是否能够从小麦,黑麦,大麦,大麦和许多其它方面中选择,它只是看家庭在面包上花费的总额而已.

p646.original: Likewise, GDP has nothing much to say about what technology and products are available. The standard of living in, for example, 1950 or 1900 was not affected only by how much money people had—it was also affected by what they could buy. No matter how much money you had in 1950, you could not buy an iPhone or a personal computer.
p646.zh: 同样,对于有哪些技术和产品,国内生产总值没有什么好说的。 例如,1950年或1900年的生活水平不仅受到人们有多少钱的影响,而且还受到他们能够购买的东西的影响。 不管你在1950年有多少钱,你都买不到iPhone或个人电脑.

p647.original: In certain cases, it is not clear that a rise in GDP is even a good thing. If a city is wrecked by a hurricane, and then experiences a surge of rebuilding construction activity, it would be peculiar to claim that the hurricane was therefore economically beneficial. If people are led by a rising fear of crime, to pay for installing bars and burglar alarms on all their windows, it is hard to believe that this increase in GDP has made them better off. Similarly, some people would argue that sales of certain goods, like pornography or extremely violent movies, do not represent a gain to society’s standard of living.
p647.zh: 在某些情况下,国内生产总值的上升甚至不是一件好事,这一点还不清楚。 如果一个城市被飓风摧毁,然后经历重建活动猛增,那么,声称飓风因此具有经济效益是一件奇事。 如果人们因为犯罪恐惧感的加剧而领头,为了在他们所有的窗户上安装酒吧和盗贼警报器而付出代价,那么很难相信国内生产总值的这种增长已经使他们的生活更加美好. 同样,有些人会认为,销售某些商品,如色情制品或极其暴力的电影,并不代表社会生活水平的提高。

p648.original: Does a Rise in GDP Overstate or Understate the Rise in the Standard of Living?
p648.zh: 国内生产总值的上升是过度夸大还是低估了生活水平的提高?

p649.original: The fact that GDP per capita does not fully capture the broader idea of standard of living has led to a concern that the increases in GDP over time are illusory. It is theoretically possible that while GDP is rising, the standard of living could be falling if human health, environmental cleanliness, and other factors that are not included in GDP are worsening. Fortunately, this fear appears to be overstated.
p649.zh: 人均国内生产总值没有充分体现更广泛的生活水平观念,这使人们担心,随着时间的推移,国内生产总值的增长是虚幻的。 在理论上,如果人类健康、环境清洁以及没有纳入国内生产总值的其他因素恶化,国内总产值在上升,生活水平可能会下降。幸运的是,这种恐惧似乎被夸大了。

p650.original: In some ways, the rise in GDP understates the actual rise in the standard of living. For example, the typical workweek for a U.S. worker has fallen over the last century from about 60 hours per week to less than 40 hours per week. Life expectancy and health have risen dramatically, and so has the average level of education. Since 1970, the air and water in the United States have generally been getting cleaner. Companies have developed new technologies for entertainment, travel, information, and health. A much wider variety of basic products like food and clothing is available today than several decades ago. Because GDP does not capture leisure, health, a cleaner environment, the possibilities that new technology creates, or an increase in variety, the actual rise in the standard of living for Americans in recent decades has exceeded the rise in GDP.
p650.zh: 在某些方面,国内生产总值的上升低估了生活水平的实际提高。 例如,美国工人的典型工作周在上个世纪从每周约60小时下降到每周不足40小时.预期寿命和健康状况急剧上升,平均教育水平也大幅上升。 自1970年以来,美国的空气和水一般越来越清洁.公司开发了娱乐、旅行、信息和卫生方面的新技术。 今天,食品和服装等基本产品种类比几十年前要广泛得多。 由于GDP不能捕捉休闲,健康,清洁的环境,新技术创造的可能性,或者品种的增加,近几十年来美国人生活水平的实际提高已经超过了GDP的上升.

p651.original: On the other side, crime rates, traffic congestion levels, and income inequality are higher in the United States now than they were in the 1960s. Moreover, a substantial number of services that women primarily provided in the non-market economy are now part of the market economy that GDP counts. By ignoring these factors, GDP would tend to overstate the true rise in the standard of living.
p651.zh: 另一方面,美国的犯罪率、交通拥堵水平和收入不平等程度都比1960年代高。 此外,妇女主要在非市场经济中提供的大量服务现在已成为国内生产总值所重视的市场经济的一部分。无视这些因素,国内生产总值往往会过分夸大生活水平的真正提高。

p652.original: Visit this website to read about the American Dream and standards of living.
p652.zh: 访问这个网站阅读"美国梦"和生活水平.

p654.original: A high level of GDP should not be the only goal of macroeconomic policy, or government policy more broadly. Even though GDP does not measure the broader standard of living with any precision, it does measure production well and it does indicate when a country is materially better or worse off in terms of jobs and incomes. In most countries, a significantly higher GDP per capita occurs hand in hand with other improvements in everyday life along many dimensions, like education, health, and environmental protection.
p654.zh: 高水平的国内生产总值不应是宏观经济政策或更广泛的政府政策的唯一目标。 尽管国内生产总值没有精确地衡量更广泛的生活水平,但它确实很好地衡量了生产,并表明一个国家在就业和收入方面在物质上是好是坏。 在大多数国家,人均国内生产总值显著提高,同时在教育、保健和环境保护等许多方面改善日常生活。

p655.original: No single number can capture all the elements of a term as broad as “standard of living.” Nonetheless, GDP per capita is a reasonable, rough-and-ready measure of the standard of living.
p655.zh: 没有一个数字能够包含“生活水平”这样宽泛的术语的所有要素。 尽管如此,人均GDP是衡量生活水平的合理、粗糙和准备程度的尺度。

p656.original: How is the Economy Doing? How Does One Tell?
p656.zh: 经济情况如何? 一个怎么告诉?

p657.original: To determine the state of the economy, one needs to examine economic indicators, such as GDP. To calculate GDP is quite an undertaking. It is the broadest measure of a nation’s economic activity and we owe a debt to Simon Kuznets, the creator of the measurement, for that.
p657.zh: 为了确定经济状况,需要审查经济指标,如国内生产总值。计算国内生产总值是一项相当艰巨的任务。 这是衡量一个国家经济活动最广泛的尺度,我们为此欠了制定计量的西蒙·库兹涅茨的债务。

p658.original: The sheer size of the U.S. economy as measured by nominal GDP is huge—as of the third quarter of 2021, $23.2 trillion worth of goods and services were produced annually. During the COVID-19-induced recession, which lasted just two months according to NBER and was concentrated across Quarters 1 and 2 of 2020, real GDP dropped 9%—much larger and quicker of a drop than during the previous economic downturn, the Great Recession (2007–2009). The economy quickly bounced back, and as of Quarter 1 of 2021, real GDP had slightly surpassed the level it was at prior to the start of the pandemic. These statistics show the severity of the pandemic-induced recession, and while real GDP fully recovered, there are other ways in which the economy has not. While GDP and GDP per capita give us a rough estimate of a nation's standard of living, there are many other ways to track the health of the economy. This chapter is the building block for other chapters that explore more economic indicators such as unemployment, inflation, or interest rates, and perhaps more importantly, will explain how they are related and what causes them to rise or fall.
p658.zh: 以名义国内生产总值衡量的美国经济规模是巨大的——截至2021年第三季度,每年生产价值23.2万亿美元的商品和服务。COVID-19引发的衰退仅持续了两个月,据NBER统计,并且集中在2020年第一和第二季度,在此期间,实际GDP比前一次经济衰退(即大衰退(2007-2010年))下降幅度大得多,下降速度更快。经济迅速回弹,截至2021年第1季度,实际GDP略高于疫情开始前的水平. 这些统计数字表明大流行病引起的衰退的严重性,虽然实际国内总产值完全恢复,但经济还有其他没有恢复的方式。 虽然国内生产总值和人均国内生产总值向我们粗略估计了一个国家的生活水平,但还有许多其他方法可以跟踪经济的健康情况。本章是探讨失业、通货膨胀或利率等更多经济指标的其他章节的组成部分,也许更重要的是,将解释这些指标如何相互关联,是什么导致它们上升或下降。

p660.original: GDP is an indicator of a society’s standard of living, but it is only a rough indicator. GDP does not directly take account of leisure, environmental quality, levels of health and education, activities conducted outside the market, changes in inequality of income, increases in variety, increases in technology, or the (positive or negative) value that society may place on certain types of output.
p660.zh: 国内生产总值是衡量一个社会生活水平的指标,但它只是粗略的指标。国内生产总值没有直接考虑到休闲、环境质量、保健和教育水平、在市场之外开展的活动、收入不平等的变化、品种的增加、技术的增加,或社会对某些类型产出可能给予的(积极或消极的)价值。

p662.original:
Explain briefly whether each of the following would cause GDP to overstate or understate the degree of change in the broad standard of living.
        
The environment becomes dirtier
The crime rate declines
A greater variety of goods become available to consumers
Infant mortality declines
p662.zh: 简单解释一下,以下每一项因素是否会导致国内生产总值过高或低估了广泛生活水平的变化程度。环境变得更加肮脏 犯罪率下降 消费者可获得的商品种类更多 婴儿死亡率下降

p663.original:
A dirtier environment would reduce the broad standard of living, but not be counted in GDP, so a rise in GDP would overstate the standard of living.
A lower crime rate would raise the broad standard of living, but not be counted directly in GDP, and so a rise in GDP would understate the standard of living.
A greater variety of goods would raise the broad standard of living, but not be counted directly in GDP, and so a rise in GDP would understate the rise in the standard of living.
A decline in infant mortality would raise the broad standard of living, but not be counted directly in GDP, and so a rise in GDP would understate the rise in the standard of living.
p663.zh: 较肮脏的环境会降低广泛的生活水平,但不计入国内生产总值,因此,国内生产总值的上升会过分夸大生活水平。降低犯罪率将提高广泛的生活水平,但不直接计入国内生产总值,因此,国内生产总值的上升将低估生活水平。更多的商品将提高广泛的生活水平,但不直接计入国内生产总值,因此,国内生产总值的上升将低估生活水平的提高。婴儿死亡率的下降将提高广泛的生活水平,但并不直接计入国内生产总值,因此,国内生产总值的上升将低估生活水平的提高。

p665.original: List some of the reasons why economists should not consider GDP an effective measure of the standard of living in a country.
p665.zh: 列出经济学家为何不把GDP视为一国生活水平的有效措施的一些原因.

p667.original: How might you measure a “green” GDP?
p667.zh: 如何衡量“绿色”国内生产总值?

c0.original: At times, such as when many people having trouble making ends meet, it is easy to tell how the economy is doing. This photograph shows people lined up during the Great Depression, waiting for relief checks. At other times, when some are doing well and others are not, it is more difficult to ascertain how the economy of a country is doing. (Credit: modification of “Waiting for relief checks. Calipatria, California” by Dorothea Lange/Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division Washington, D.C. 20540 USA, Public Domain)
c0.zh: 有时,比如,当许多人难以糊口时,很容易知道经济是如何发展的。 这张照片显示,人们在大萧条期间排队,等待救济检查. 在另一些情况下,当一些国家表现良好,而另一些国家表现不佳时,就更难确定一个国家的经济如何发展。(编辑:修改了“等待救济检查。由多罗西亚·兰格/国会印刷和摄影司图书馆撰写,华盛顿特区。20540 美国,公共域名).

c1.original: This chart shows what macroeconomics is about. The box on the left indicates a consensus of what are the most important goals for the macro economy, the middle box lists the frameworks economists use to analyze macroeconomic changes (such as inflation or recession), and the box on the right indicates the two tools the federal government uses to influence the macro economy.
c1.zh: 这张图表显示了宏观经济的本质.左边的盒子表示对什么是宏观经济最重要的目标的共识,中间的盒子列出经济学家用来分析宏观经济变化(如通货膨胀或衰退)的框架经济学家,右边的盒子表示联邦政府用来影响宏观经济的两个工具.

c3.original: Consumption makes up over half of the demand side components of the GDP. Totals in the chart do not add to 100% because the Net Export Expenditure, Exports minus Imports, is actually a negative 3.1%, as shown in . (Source: http://bea.gov/iTable/index_nipa.cfm, Table 1.1.10)
c3.zh: 消费占国内生产总值需求部分的一半以上。表中的总数没有增加100%,因为出口净支出减去进口实际上为负3.1%,如上所示。(资料来源:http://bea.gov/itable/index_nipa.cfm,表1.1.10)

c4.original: (a) Consumption is about two-thirds of GDP, and it has been on a slight upward trend over time. Business investment hovers around 15% of GDP, but it fluctuates more than consumption. Government spending on goods and services is slightly under 20% of GDP and has declined modestly over time. (b) Exports are added to total demand for goods and services, while imports are subtracted from total demand. If exports exceed imports, as in most of the 1960s and 1970s in the U.S. economy, a trade surplus exists. If imports exceed exports, as in recent years, then a trade deficit exists. (Source: http://bea.gov/iTable/index_nipa.cfm, Table 1.1.10)
c4.zh: (a) 消费约占国内生产总值的三分之二,一段时间以来,消费呈略微上升趋势。商业投资徘徊在国内生产总值的15%左右,但波动大于消费。 政府用于货物和服务的支出略低于国内生产总值的20%,并随着时间的推移略有下降。(b) 将出口与货物和服务总需求相加,而进口从总需求中扣除。 如果出口超过进口,如1960年代和1970年代美国经济的大部分,则存在贸易顺差。 如果进口超过出口,就存在贸易逆差。(资料来源:http://bea.gov/itable/index_nipa.cfm,表1.1.10)

c6.original: Services make up over 60 percent of the production side components of GDP in the United States.
c6.zh: 服务业占美国国内生产总值生产部分的60%以上。

c7.original: Services are the largest single component of total supply, representing over 60 percent  of GDP, up from about 45 percent in the early 1950s. Durable and nondurable goods constitute the manufacturing sector, and they have declined from 40 percent of GDP in 1950 to about 30 percent in 2016. Nondurable goods used to be larger than durable goods, but in recent years, nondurable goods have been dropping to below the share of  durable goods, which is less than  20% of GDP. Structures hover around 10% of GDP. We do not show here the change in inventories, the final component of aggregate supply. It is typically less than 1% of GDP.
c7.zh: 服务业是供应总量中最大的单一部分,占国内生产总值的60%以上,比1950年代初期的45%左右有所上升。持久和不可持久商品构成制造业部门,它们从1950年占国内生产总值的40%下降到2016年的30%左右。 非耐用商品曾经大于耐用商品,但近年来,非耐用商品一直下降到耐用商品比重以下,低于GDP的20%.结构徘徊在国内生产总值的10%左右。 我们在此没有显示库存的变化,即总供应的最后组成部分。 它通常不到国内生产总值的1%。

c10.original: Nominal GDP values have risen exponentially from 1960 through 2020, according to the BEA.
c10.zh: 根据《北京行动纲要》,1960年至2020年名义国内生产总值值呈指数上升趋势。

c11.original: Much like nominal GDP, the GDP deflator has risen exponentially from 1960 through 2010. (Source: BEA https://apps.bea.gov/itable/index.cfm, Table 1.1.9)
c11.zh: 与名义国内生产总值一样,1960年至2010年,国内生产总值的缩减指数呈指数增长。(资料来源:BEA https://apps.bea.gov/itable/index.cfm,表1.1.9)

c13.original: The red line measures U.S. GDP in nominal dollars. The black line measures U.S. GDP in real dollars, where all dollar values are converted to 2012 dollars. Since we express real GDP in 2012 dollars, the two lines cross in 2012. However, real GDP will appear higher than nominal GDP in the years before 2012, because dollars were worth less in 2012 than in previous years. Conversely, real GDP will appear lower in the years after 2012, because dollars were worth more in 2012 than in later years.
c13.zh: 红线测量美国.以名义美元计的GDP.黑线测量美国.以实值计的GDP,所有美元值均折算为2012年美元. 由于我们以2012年美元表示实际GDP,2012年两条线横跨. 然而,2012年之前的年份,实际国内生产总值似乎将高于名义国内生产总值,因为2012年美元的价值低于往年。 相反,2012年以后的年份,实际国内生产总值将较低,因为2012年美元的价值比后些年高。

c16.original: Real GDP in the United States in 2020 (in 2012 dollars) was about $18.4 trillion. After adjusting to remove the effects of inflation, this represents a roughly 20-fold increase in the economy’s production of goods and services since 1930. (Source: bea.gov)
c16.zh: 2020年美国实际GDP(以2012年美元计)约为18.4万亿美元. 在作出调整以消除通货膨胀的影响之后,这相当于自1930年以来经济的货物和服务生产增加了大约20倍。(资料来源:bea.gov)
